question.text: Kaveri Opportunities Fund, a Category II AIF with total corpus INR 800 crore and estimated lifetime administrative/management expenses of INR 40 crore, is evaluating a buyout in Apex Realty Ltd. What is the maximum amount it may deploy in this single investee company under the standard Cat II concentration rule?

answer.text: INR 190 crore (25% of investable funds, i.e. corpus net of fund expenses)
INR 400 crore (50% limit applicable to all Cat II AIFs)

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 15(1)(c) caps investment by a Cat I/II AIF in a single investee company at 25% of INVESTABLE FUNDS, not 25% of corpus. Investable funds = Corpus – estimated administration/management expenses for the life of the fund. Here: Investable funds = 800 – 40 = INR 760 crore; 25% of 760 = INR 190 crore. The Trap: Option A applies 25% to the gross corpus (common shortcut error — ignores the 'investable funds' definition in Reg 15). Option C uses the 50% LVF carve-out, which applies only to Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors. Option D confuses with the Cat I temporary-borrowing 10% ceiling. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A Distributors test the number as '25% single investee cap'. XIX-C tests both the 25% (Cat I/II) and 10% (Cat III) caps. XIX-E Cat III uses the 10% cap on listed securities — different number entirely. Not to be confused with SEBI (Mutual Funds) 10% single-issuer cap. Manager's Pro-Tip: At IC level, treat 25% as the absolute regulatory ceiling but target 15-18% as internal soft cap — gives cushion for follow-on rounds, pro-rata bridge commitments and write-ups. LVFs for AI investors can stretch to 50% single-investee; useful for concentrated family-office style portfolios.
